# Page 2^page=2
Challenges of this module Let us suppose we are facing a problem for which exact algorithms are impractical: very short time available very difﬁcult problem Can we propose fast but approximate solution methods? What is the role of the exact methods seen so far? Can we ﬁnd some general algorithmic structures that can be adapted in an easy way to a variety of problems? We have already used these general algorithmic structures

Recall the main steps of the augmenting path algorithm Recall the main steps of the LP algorithm What do they have in common?

# Page 4^page=4
Facing difﬁcult problems When can we say that a problem is “difﬁcult”? Find the exact optimal solution (potentially in an exponential time) Find a good solution in a reasonable time (but not provably optimal) Heuristic algorithms Exploit the problem structure Produce good solutions Fast

# Page 15^page=15
Local Search Start with a feasible solution Try to improve the current solution by making “small changes” Stop if no improvement is found The obtained solution is a so called “Local Optimum”
